elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall...", covering both trigger events.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted language provides assistance "for at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period is stated. To meet the preferred level the drafter must render "up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis appears in the inserted sentence; the words "at Kubient's then-current rates" are absent.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Customer all data of Customer in Kubient's possession or control."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The export obligation specifies no format; "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" is missing.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No post-return deletion or written certification obligation is inserted; retained clause 4(c)(iv) only addresses return-or-destruction of Confidential Information without certification.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason" anchors both the assistance and export obligations to every covered ending; the request condition is not tied to anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days" — meets the 90-day floor; the Customer-request trigger mirrors the model language and is within Customer's control.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Customer all data of Customer in Kubient's possession or control" — deadline runs from the termination/expiry event, not from a request.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: all three fallback elements are satisfied in operative language inserted into the termination section (Section 4(c)), so the position is complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level is not complete: the clause omits the six-month assistance period, then-current-rates pricing, machine-readable format, and certified deletion after return. The comment correctly discloses that it targets the fallback.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion into a clause that previously supplied nothing on transition or data return; no existing Customer-favourable language (including the mutual return/destroy of Confidential Information in 4(c)(iv)) was deleted or paraphrased, and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense language, or additional procedures were added.

Intent preserved: the insertion sits alongside the existing effects-of-termination list without contradicting the cessation of Services, revocation of the licence, or the Confidential Information return/destroy obligation, and leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference. Minor drafting note only (not a defect at the fallback level): retained 4(c)(iv) lets a Party destroy the other's Confidential Information, so consider adding "subject to Kubient's export obligation below" if Customer data is treated as Confidential Information.

If we later push to preferred, the operative repairs needed are: change "at least ninety (90) days" to "up to six (6) months at Kubient's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export obligation, and add a clause requiring deletion and written certification thereafter.
